newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia should discount gas domestically - Nemtsov.
newsitem.headline: Russia should discount gas domestically - Nemtsov.

text.p: Russia should sell its gas at lower prices domestically to help out its struggling industry, Interfax news agency quoted First Deputy Prime Minister Boris Nemtsov as saying on Sunday.
"Since the production of Russian industry is not competitive today, we cannot sell gas inside Russia at world prices," Nemtsov said during a visit to Yamburg in Siberia.
The pricing of gas domestically should "raise the economy on one hand and increase enterprises' ability to pay on the other", said Nemtsov, who is also fuel and energy minister.

Nemtsov on Thursday was quoted as saying that Russia will soon cut the wholesale price of high-pressure natural gas by 30 percent. Nemtsov said Rem Vyakhirev, chairman of Russian gas monopoly Gazprom, had agreed to the change, Interfax quoted him as saying.
Lower gas prices will also prove helpful for Gazprom because they will enable Russian firms to actually pay for the gas they receive rather than pile up huge debts, Nemtsov said.
"Simply speaking, gas for cash is cheap and efficient. Gas for barter -- such as for T shirts and underwear that no one needs -- is expensive and inefficient," he said.
Those Russian firms unable to pay for their gas, he said, should face the spectre of bankruptcy.
Russian firms own Gasprom 70 trillion roubles ($12 billion), Itar-Tass news agency quoted Nemtsov as saying.
